host_initial_failure.disposition: Failed actual identity race observation retained. Bounded body detachment passes deterministic delayed-writer/fault tests and twenty focused race repetitions plus the full lab race suite. Native execution is separate and has no race instrumentation.

attempts.native: Fresh run from signed repaired candidate; unchanged 3600 guest/2400 build/1200 patch ceilings and all authentication/native/traffic/cleanup assertions. No host executable fallback.

native_initial_failure.disposition: Compiled native outputs/163 ordinary cases passed, but api-stall returned empty 200/one effect instead of 502/one effect. The source adds explicit request-context/deadline admission after response EOF and six deterministic response-boundary cases; all existing time/effect assertions stay unchanged.

findings.identity: Ten direct uncontained TLS component rows use actual test-only Coraza REMOTE_ADDR/REMOTE_PORT rules to distinguish default transport identity from opt-in source metadata. Spoofed forwarding headers do not select identity; benign body/header effects, CRS denial, authority checks and internal route replacement/rollback retain exact outcomes. Six context and five body-lifetime/fault subtests pass separately.
findings.cli: The actual guarded CLI accepts TLS+identity check-only, rejects identity without TLS before binding, and separately passes the normal-CRS 44-case/four-phase relayd/PF matrix with one enabled-mode receipt per phase. No synthetic rule-file CLI, identity response endpoint or product address logging is added.
findings.trust: The flag asserts an externally maintained sender boundary. The process neither authenticates PROXY nor installs/verifies PF; open/rollback forged-prefix controls remain reachable. Root/PF administrators and allowed-UID compromise are outside this boundary.
findings.body_ownership: The new tests exposed Coraza transaction-buffer cleanup racing the backend transport writer. The adapter now bounds, consumes/closes and detaches inspected body bytes before RoundTrip, preserving framing metadata and rejecting read/close/size/length faults before the backend. No dependency/upstream patch.
findings.rollback: Startup-only identity selection persists across internal route replacement/rollback; disabling requires stop/restart. Both PF modes independently restore all eight static views, preserve known good after invalid replacement and clean all peers/keys/listeners before verified VM teardown.
findings.response_budget: The retained first native attempt exposed empty 200 for the stalled HTTPS backend at 2.13 seconds. Response buffering now independently rejects cancelled/expired caller context even after clean EOF; the original two-second budget and 502/one-effect expectation are unchanged.

limitations: The actual Coraza identity-rule component server is direct and uncontained, with test-only directives/internal route replacement. The actual CLI uses the normal pinned CRS rules in its separate relayd/PF matrix; it has no injected identity-rule probe or address-observation endpoint. Do not collapse these evidence scopes.
Fresh IPv4 PROXY v1/companion TLS and close-only HTTP/1.1 lab profile only. Default mode retains transport identity. Missing/invalid metadata fails closed only in the opt-in path.

No backend identity headers, backend isolation, remote cryptographic authentication, existing-state revocation, production startup/privilege policy, certificate operations or audit-redaction acceptance. Lab PF templates pass other traffic/backend ports.

Host race results are distinct from native execution. Advisory scans do not establish memory/lifecycle safety; the initially observed race remains failed evidence despite earlier passing scans/race runs.
Caddy retains its existing CEL package-only and unimported OpenPGP module-only residuals; it is not rerun or declared equivalent here. No full selected-graph clean claim.
Full CRS/application tuning, persistent/streaming/protocol parity, hard resource/soak budgets, image/daemon lineage, distribution and product adoption remain open.

No live network, persistent service, release, installer schema, architecture selection or separate connector API/repository change. Private keys, raw logs/configuration and complete source inventories stay ignored.
